title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in 'variations sur l'équation des lacets', Grothendieck replaces the universal case Ĝ⁺ = (GL(2,Z))^, Ĝ^♮ = Π₀ (see the next page) by an abstract profinite group G_{ρ,σ}. It comes with two distinguished elements: ρ, of 'order 3' type, and σ, of 'order 2' type, the images of the standard elliptic generators of (P)SL₂(Z). For x = ρ, σ:
- N_x is the normalizer of ⟨x⟩.
- Z_x is the centralizer of x.
- SZ_x is a 'special' centralizer, apparently the part inside a distinguished normal subgroup 𝔊.
- Γ_{ρ,σ} is a quotient group, written γ_{ρ,σ} on this page.
- δ_x : N_x → Γ_{ρ,σ} is surjective with kernel SZ_x.
On the previous page (60) he defined N_x^♮, Z_x^♮, SZ_x^♮ as the intersections with a subgroup G^♮_{ρ,σ}. He also wrote the exact sequences (61): 1 → SZ_x^♮ → N_x^♮ → Γ_{ρ,σ} → 1.

This page writes out the 'morphismes de suites exactes' he announced.

(62) For x = ρ, σ: the inclusion of 1 → SZ_x^♮ → N_x^♮ → Γ → 1 into 1 → SZ_x → N_x → Γ → 1, with the identity on Γ. This says δ_x is already surjective on the ♮-part.

(63) Each N_x carries a sign character recording how it acts on its distinguished element (x ↦ x^{±1}):
- ε_{3ρ} : N_ρ → μ (μ = {±1}), with kernel Z_ρ.
- ε_{2σ} : N_σ → μ, with kernel Z_σ.
These characters factor through δ as ε_{3γ}, ε_{2γ} : Γ → μ. Their kernels are Γ' and Γ'' respectively. Hence the vertical maps Z_ρ^♮ → Γ'_{ρ,σ} and Z_σ^♮ → Γ''_{ρ,σ} are epimorphisms, with kernels SZ_x^♮.

(64) A summary diagram:
- Main row: the extension 1 → 𝔊^♮ → G^♮_{ρ,σ} → Γ_{ρ,σ} → 1.
- Mapping into it: L₀^♮ = SZ_{ρ,σ} ↪ Z_{ρ,σ}, SZ_ρ^♮ ↪ N_ρ^♮ and SZ_σ^♮ ↪ N_σ^♮. The SZ's go into 𝔊^♮ and the N's and Z_{ρ,σ} go into G^♮_{ρ,σ}.
- Characters of Γ: ε_{3γ}, ε_{2γ} to μ and a cyclotomic-type character χ_γ to Ẑ*.
- Below: the reference row 1 → 𝔊⁺ → 𝔊 → μ₂ → 1, compared with the top row by vertical arrows (cf. p. 581', (45)).

Purpose: build an axiomatic 'ρ,σ-group' framework that imitates the structure of (GL₂(Z))^ and its normalizers of elliptic elements. This serves the study of the loop equation (the GT-type relations) and its 'twisted' variants. The next page shows the immediate snag: Z_{ρ,σ} is too big, and a subgroup Z_{ρ,σ}(0) must be split off.
errors: No mathematical error is visible; the diagrams are bookkeeping that follows formally from (61) once ε factors through δ.
The surjectivity of Z^♮ → Γ' needs ε_{3ρ}^♮ to factor through δ_ρ^♮. This is implicit and requires SZ_ρ ⊂ Z_ρ, which holds by definition.

In (64) the precise vertical maps between the bottom row (𝔊⁺ → 𝔊 → μ₂) and the top row are partly crossed out and ambiguous. The arrow between μ₂ and Γ_{ρ,σ} is drawn double-headed, so the exact relation is unclear.

ideas.what: Exact sequences 1 → SZ_x → N_x → Γ_{ρ,σ} → 1 for the normalizers of the order-2 and order-3 elliptic elements, and their restriction to a subgroup G^♮
ideas.modern_name: normalizers/centralizers of torsion elements in profinite completions of SL₂(Z)/GL₂(Z); outer-type quotients
ideas.usually_credited_to: Related to work on GT and (P)SL₂(Z) by Drinfeld, Ihara, Lochak–Schneps and Nakamura (1990s)
ideas.where_published: Not in Esquisse; this is unpublished Longue Marche continuation material

ideas.what: Sign characters ε₂, ε₃ (action on the elliptic generator by inversion) and a cyclotomic character χ on Γ_{ρ,σ}
ideas.modern_name: cyclotomic character and orientation characters on GT-type groups

ideas.what: Axiomatization of a 'ρ,σ-group' G_{ρ,σ} with a ♮-subgroup that imitates (GL₂(Z))^ ⊃ Π₀
ideas.modern_name: abstract framework for twisted loop equations / GT-like groups

missed.claim: Part of an unpublished axiomatic framework (groups G_{ρ,σ} with distinguished elliptic elements and a ♮-subgroup) generalizing the (GL₂(Z))^ setting of the loop equation. The next page shows it was not yet satisfactory, because Z_{ρ,σ} is too big.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It might interest people studying generalized GT groups. This page itself is routine diagram bookkeeping.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is formal bookkeeping: morphisms of exact sequences that follow from the previous page's definitions. The surrounding framework is unpublished but not especially surprising.
transcription_corrections: The quotient written γ_{ρ,σ} throughout is the same Γ_{ρ,σ} as on the previous page; the handwriting looks like a script gamma.
The superscript transcribed as 𝔖 is the ♮/𝔊-type decoration of the previous page (intersection with G^♮_{ρ,σ}).
In the second diagram of (63) the bottom map Γ'' → Γ → μ has no label; it should be ε_{2γ}. Its right vertical arrow is a plain ↓.
In (64) the bottom row reads 1 → 𝔊⁺ → 𝔊 → μ₂ → 1, with vertical arrows up to 𝔊^♮, G^♮_{ρ,σ} and Γ_{ρ,σ}.
There is a small marginal annotation '636' (or 'δ36') above N_ρ^♮ at the top of the page, possibly a page reference.
